what: Affiliated Managers Group buys minority stakes in boutique asset managers and takes a share of their revenue, leaving the founders running their own firms.
customers: Through its affiliates, pension funds, wealthy individuals and institutions investing in specialist strategies.
money: a contracted share of each affiliate's management fees
a share of incentive fees on alternative strategies
moat: Contracts that give AMG a fixed share of revenue before the affiliate's own costs, which makes it unusually profitable, while the affiliates keep the independence that retains their talent.
risks: Traditional active management keeps losing assets to index funds
Revenue declined from $2.4B to $2.0B before stabilising
opportunities: 13.3 times earnings and 8.1 times free cash flow with a 34.5% net margin
Analysts see about 24% upside, with 7 covering the stock
The portfolio has been shifted toward private markets and alternatives, where fees are not under the same pressure
watch: Net client flows at the affiliates and the mix shift toward alternatives.
